latest_release.body:
# v3.5

v3.5 is mostly a fix-and-polish release after the big v3.4.  We burned down the open issues backlog, and out of that came a rebuilt PostgreSQL loader, a new native DuckDB loader, and three security fixes.

## Security fixes

Nine people reported three security issues in VisiData (eight of them found the same zip slip):

- **pandas**: `.pickle` files are no longer loaded unless the new `pandas_allow_pickle` option is set (default off).  Unpickling runs arbitrary code from the file, so opening an untrusted `.pickle` could execute it.  CVE pending, reported by @Santoshkumarpuppala.
- **unzip_http**: refuse zip members whose path resolves outside the extraction directory (Zip Slip).  CVE-2026-41958, reported by @MaxFreedomPollard, and independently by @robsherw of Cisco Talos and six others.  Also fixed in [unzip-http](https://github.com/saulpw/unzip-http) 0.8.
- **eml**: `gx` refuses attachment filenames that resolve outside the extraction directory (path traversal).  CVE-2026-42532, reported by @robsherw of Cisco Talos.

You should upgrade if you open files from sources you don't trust.

## Data changes

- Dict and list cells now save as JSON by default in text formats. (#2944)
- On the Describe sheet, all null forms count as one distinct value. (#3223)

## Interface changes

- **Join** type `concat` matches columns by position and keeps the first sheet's column names (and type as before).  Use `append` to match by name. (#3208)
- **Macros** record literal `{braces}` safely (f-strings and regexes no longer turn into parameters), and `{{ }}` escapes braces in parameterized macros. (#2785)
- **Command line args** are now added in order @midichef (#3225)
- **Options**: reading an undefined option warns and returns None, instead of raising.

## New commands

- `set-envvar` to record environment changes for replay (for e.g. $LC_ALL reproducibility). (#3195)
- `addcol-incr-key`, like `addcol-incr` but increment restarts at each change in key columns
- `select-col-duplicates` to select duplicate cells in one column @midichef
- `resize-col-max-all` and `resize-cols-max-all` to resize columns looking at all rows (#2780)
- `syscopy-sql` (#2393)
- `undo-redo-input` (`zU`) undoes the last change and reruns it with its input prefilled, for e.g. fixing a typo in a long expression. (#3031)
- `llm-query-sheet` and `llm-query-selected` send rows as one query to an Anthropic LLM; stream replies into the sheet (#2947)

## Highlighted features

- **PostgreSQL loader overhaul**: open a table directly with `postgres://host/dbname/tablename`, run `exec-sql`/`edit-sql`, and browse large tables that load lazily and stream rows.  Connection details come from libpq (via `$PGUSER`, `$PGHOST`, `~/.pgpass`, etc).  Tables are readonly for now; write support is deferred to a later release. (#282 #586 #727 #2989)
- **Native DuckDB loader** for `.duckdb` files, including saver. (#3035 #3237)
- **Decimal type**: `type-decimal` parses currency and `(1,234.50)` accounting negatives and keeps the source precision.  Unbound by default; bind it to `$` to try it. (#2396)
- **Command-server client**: include the `vdx` script to interact with a live `vd` command-server (LLMs can drive vd now too!)
- **.vds format**: several improvements to VisiData's own save format

## Spit and Polish

- **Hidden columns** keep their width across hide/unhide; sheet edge requires extra `go-right` before stepping into hidden columns. (#3214 #3215)
- **Better wide-character support**: fix terminal display issues with emoji and wide characters, and also better wrapping for same. (#2416 #2685)
- **Archives**: members decompress by suffix, nested tars open, and `zEnter` opens a member as a chosen filetype. (#3212)
- **macOS**: respect `XDG_DATA_HOME`/`XDG_STATE_HOME` on macOS

Thanks to @midichef for many bugfixes and reviews, and to @VXNCXNX, @danielwe, @chutzimir, @mpr1255, @horizonbymuneeb, @chiliec, @dacodas, @maxfain, and @khughi

# VisiData v3.5

[![Tests](https://github.com/saulpw/visidata/workflows/visidata-ci-build/badge.svg)](https://github.com/saulpw/visidata/actions/workflows/main.yml)
[![Gitpod ready-to-code](https://img.shields.io/badge/Gitpod-ready--to--code-blue?logo=gitpod)](https://gitpod.io/#https://github.com/saulpw/visidata)

[![discord](https://img.shields.io/discord/880915750007750737?label=discord)](https://visidata.org/chat)
[![Mastodon](https://img.shields.io/mastodon/follow/110136431814047095?domain=https%3A%2F%2Ffosstodon.org)](https://fosstodon.org/@saulpw)

A terminal interface for exploring and arranging tabular data.

![Frequency table](http://visidata.org/videos/freq-move-row.gif)

VisiData supports tsv, csv, sqlite, json, xlsx (Excel), hdf5, and [many other formats](https://visidata.org/formats).

## Platform requirements

- Linux, OS/X, or Windows (with WSL)
- Python 3.8+
- additional Python modules are required for certain formats and sources

## Install

To install the latest release from PyPi:

    pip3 install visidata

To try VisiData without installing, use [pipx](https://pipx.pypa.io/) or [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/):

    pipx run visidata          # or: uvx visidata

To install permanently (adds `vd` to your PATH):

    pipx install visidata      # or: uv tool install visidata

Additional Python packages are needed for some formats:

    pipx install visidata --preinstall openpyxl --preinstall lxml
    # or: uv tool install visidata --with openpyxl --with lxml

To add format packages to an existing pipx install:

    pipx inject visidata openpyxl lxml

To install the cutting edge `develop` branch (no warranty expressed or implied):

    pip3 install git+https://github.com/saulpw/visidata.git@develop

If VisiData reports `package X not installed` even after you installed it, `vd`
is almost certainly running from a different environment than the one you
installed the package into. Check `which vd`, then install the package into
*that* environment — e.g. `pipx inject visidata X` for a pipx install, or the
Homebrew Python for `brew install visidata`.

See [visidata.org/install](https://visidata.org/install) for detailed instructions for all available platforms and package managers.

### Usage

    $ vd <input>
    $ <command> | vd

Press `Ctrl+Q` to quit at any time.

Hundreds of other commands and options are also available; see the documentation.

### Documentation

* [VisiData documentation](https://visidata.org/docs)
* [Plugin Author's Guide and API Reference](https://visidata.org/docs/api)
* [Quick reference](https://visidata.org/man) (available within `vd` with `Ctrl+H`), which has a list of commands and options.
* [Intro to VisiData Tutorial](https://jsvine.github.io/intro-to-visidata/) by [Jeremy Singer-Vine](https://www.jsvine.com/)

### Help and Support

If you have a question, issue, or suggestion regarding VisiData, please [create an issue on Github](https://github.com/saulpw/visidata/issues) or chat with us at #visidata on [irc.libera.chat](https://libera.chat/).

If you use VisiData regularly, please [support me on Patreon](https://www.patreon.com/saulpw)!

## License

Code in the `stable` branch of this repository, including the main `vd` application, loaders, and plugins, is available for use and redistribution under GPLv3.

## Credits

VisiData is conceived and developed by Saul Pwanson `<vd@saul.pw>`.

Anja Kefala `<anja.kefala@gmail.com>` maintains the documentation and packages for all platforms.

Many thanks to numerous other [contributors](https://visidata.org/credits/), and to those wonderful users who provide feedback, for helping to make VisiData the awesome tool that it is.
